I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I am reviewing my current assets. I have $1314 cash and am on NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE. Most of my properties are mortgaged, though the pinks and oranges are fully built with four houses each. I also hold two Get Out of Jail Free cards.

I just purchased North Carolina Avenue for $21. The opponent has only $20 cash and sits on Park Place. I am the last player with assets remaining. The bank has no houses left, so I can safely build hotels.

I will not build hotels on the pinks or oranges. Hotels return four houses to the bank, which would help the opponent build on reds. I also will not unmortgage properties or trade away key assets like Park Place, the GOOJF cards, or cash. My $1314 buffer covers the $750 rent on Illinois with three houses. The pinks and oranges are already fully built, so there is nothing left to upgrade.

Marvin Gardens and North Carolina are incomplete monopolies, so building is impossible there. I will not mortgage or unmortgage anything; I have enough cash and no houses to build.

I will end my turn. The opponent has no assets I need, and trading would only help them.

I corrected the rent on Illinois Avenue with three houses to $850, not $750. I still have enough cash to cover it. I am also confirming that this is a post-turn action after the opponent ended their turn.
